about: Input for the update prompt on the Updates page. Report changes; do not edit.

field_notes.tools_checked: The day the Meta pages behind the tool list were last read.
field_notes.use: Whether an account used a tool is always the 12 months to 22 Nov 2026. The One Big Table download (tools.csv) uses that window in its column names.
field_notes.rank: A popularity rank is a score from public sources that name the tool, not measured use.
field_notes.ad_set_counts: An ad-set count 'X of N': for VN, N is the top 40 ad sets by spend; for US, N is all 19 ad sets by spend. A share of spend is the spend of the counted ad sets divided by the spend of all the ad sets in N.

branches: Creative and placement: what do people see, where?
Bidding and budget: where does the money go?
After the click: what happens next?
Profit: does the spend make money?
Running the account: access, policy, tools (added)
stages: Delivery (who saw it, at what cost)

group.rule: Each tool sits in exactly one of 7 groups, as set in the feature map. The map was built from Meta for Business pages and the Meta developer docs, read 22 November 2026. Groups are ordered by their best-ranked tool: the group that holds the top-ranked tool comes first. A tie goes to the group with the higher total score. Group size does not decide.
group.excludes: Inside a group, ranked tools come first by rank; tools with fewer than 2 public sources are not ranked and keep Meta's page order.

branch.rule: The issue-tree question the tool mainly helps answer. If it helps two, it goes to the one earlier in the money chain: tracking, audience, creative, bidding, after the click, profit.
branch.excludes: 'Running the account' holds only access, policy and admin tools, which never move sales directly.

benefit.rule: The profit lever the tool is built to move: more sales, cheaper sales, true numbers, a safe account or less work.
benefit.excludes: A tool judged by a cost metric but built to win results (the campaign goals, lookalikes, formats) keeps 'more sales'. 'Cheaper sales' is listed as its second lever.

stage.rule: The funnel stage of the tool's main metric: delivery, attention, conversion, value, profit; or signal and account health. A metric that names two stages takes the later one.
stage.excludes: The earlier stage is kept as the tool's second stage. Reporting, API and account-health tools take 'signal and account health' even when their metric names a funnel stage; each is listed with a reason.

prompt:
You are checking "The Meta Ads Universe": 115 Meta ads tools, last checked 22 Nov 2026. The latest change confirmed on a Meta page is 12 Oct 2025. The latest change reported anywhere is 12 Nov 2026, by a vendor blog only.
Input: attach the file update-package.json (download it with the "Download update package" link on the Updates page). If you cannot attach files, open it at the address where this file was published. It holds the 115 tools (name, group, what it does, source link), the 58 Meta source pages, the 7 groups, the rules to sort a tool (branch, benefit, stage) and the rules below.
1. Open every source page.
2. Open these 2 change logs: https://developers.facebook.com/docs/marketing-api/marketing-api-changelog and https://developers.facebook.com/docs/graph-api/changelog.
3. Note each change made after 22 Nov 2026.
4. For each new, changed or removed ads tool, write one line: name, new/changed/removed, group (one of the 7), what it does, source link, date.
5. Rule: every tool has exactly 1 group.
6. Rule: a new tool's use is 'not sure' until someone checks the ad account.
7. Rule: rank a tool only if 2 or more public sources name it.
Before you report a line, check four things.
- The link opens on a Meta page.
- The date is after the last check.
- The group exists.
- A new tool is not in the package yet. A changed or removed tool names its entry in the package.
Output: a change report only. You cannot edit the demo or the ad accounts.
A maintainer applies the report. The maintainer sorts each new tool into a branch, benefit and stage, then re-runs the demo's checks.
